findings.text: Guess-mode unwinder exposes a return-address-pointer query that always reports absence, indicating this engine cannot locate a writable return slot.

Table-driven unwinder exposes a return-address-pointer query that reports absence when finished, otherwise yields the current instruction field when register-backed, or the word below the current stack position when stack-backed.
Both unwind engines expose a frame-advance operation returning progress indication, with negative meaning finished or failed and affirmative meaning state now describes the older caller frame.

Guess stepping scans the current stack extent word by word for values that reside in kernel text, advancing on first match, otherwise aligning to the following stack range and refreshing the extent description until no range remains.
Table-driven stepping holds a scoped read-side guard across table lookup and frame derivation so module metadata cannot disappear mid-read.

Table-driven stepping ends immediately for user-mode register state and distinguishes signal versus call addresses for table lookup, falling back to a frame-pointer assumption marked as erroneous when no entry exists, while undefined entries fail and end-of-stack entries terminate normally.

Prior stack position is recovered from a table-selected base with direct and indirect variants plus several temporary holding registers, where missing register values or unknown bases cause failure with diagnostic, and indirect forms add offset after dereference.

Caller instruction and stack values are recovered according to entry kind, with plain calls loading from below the prior stack and clearing register linkage, full register blocks loading both values and recording a full view, and partial interrupt frames loading from a smaller area while preserving prior linkage when appropriate, including return and hook adjustments.

Base pointer recovery follows table selection with undefined preserving prior register content when available and two dereference forms otherwise, and stepping rejects same-stack non-advancing results as corrupt to avoid loops, marking failure.
Diagnostics use deferred once-only warnings, with an additional current-task-only wrapper that suppresses repeats after error and optionally dumps state a single time when debugging is enabled.

Address resolution maps zero to a null entry, uses a block-indexed table for main kernel text with index and range validation, searches init text slowly over the whole table, and locates entries by rightmost-duplicate binary search over delta-encoded addresses that tolerate section terminators.

After kernel tables, resolution consults module tables when present, then frame-pointer assumption for just-in-time code with that property, then trampoline-aware lookup that maps copied code back to its template while avoiding self-recursion, with build-dependent empty variants that always miss.

Stack reads are validated against the current extent, refreshing the extent for the target when needed and revalidating, covering single words and full or partial register areas, with 32-bit full-register support explicitly rejected at build time.

General register retrieval requires a current register view, serving directly from the full view when present, otherwise from preserved prior linkage when in partial view, else reporting unavailability.

Observed unwind state carries current stack and instruction and base positions, present and prior register views plus a fullness flag, signal and error and completion indicators, owning task identity, and current stack extent with visited mask.

Observed table entry carries kind and signal marker plus stack-base selector with offset and base-pointer selector with offset, while observed stack extent carries bounds and following position with type tag.

Observed boot video metadata includes per-card safety flag with probe and mode count and table and setter plus exceptional range and name, per-mode dimensions with identifier and depth, and screen state with origin and cursor flags and geometry.

Boot video setup provides the early display configuration entry that prepares heap, captures initial parameters, preserves screen contents, probes safe cards, resolves requested mode interactively, records canonical result, captures display identity, refreshes parameters, and conditionally restores contents.
Card discovery is idempotent per safety class, invoking each matching card probe once to populate its mode count and leaving unscanned classes for later on-demand scan.

Mode activation treats current as no-op, maps two legacy aliases to standard choices, delegates to raw resolver, applies vertical recalculation when requested, and persists the canonical identifier for later kernel use except in wakeup builds.

Raw resolution ignores the recalculation request for matching, prefers visible probed entries by menu position or fixed identifier or resolution encoding, then accepts unprobed exceptional ranges via synthetic hidden descriptors, otherwise signals failure.

Vertical timing recomputation derives visible lines from firmware font height and row count with forced overrides, then unlocks and programs low and overflow portions of the timing registers through indexed access.
Status read at 0x3CC selects control base 0x3D4 versus 0x3B4, indexed reads use index write then data read while writes combine both, and text segment is 0xB000 for monochrome mode 0x07 else 0xB800.

Video queries use interrupt 0x10 with cursor and mode subfunctions and VBE DDC subfunction 0x4F15 gated on version 2.0, keyboard uses interrupt 0x16 with blocking and pending subfunctions where pending is absence of zero flag, and time uses interrupt 0x1A subfunction for seconds.

Display identity area is prefilled with 0x13, left as prefilled when version or status 0x004F checks fail, otherwise overwritten by firmware block read into boot parameters, with whole handling omitted when firmware-data support is disabled.

Mode prompting drains input, waits a bounded interval distinguishing continue versus listing requests with audible feedback for other keys, then repeatedly shows available modes and accepts direct selection or triggers unsafe rescan before reprompting.

Input helpers drain until quiescent, provide blocking character read and nonblocking pending test, and implement bounded wait by polling pending against second-resolution clock ticks with count 30 returning distinguished timeout value.

Menu selection edits up to four characters with backspace support, treats empty as current, accumulates hexadecimal value with case folding, and listing shows only visible entries with adaptive column count and sequential key labels.

Guess stepping can accept coincidental kernel-text values as frames and ORC stepping marks output unreliable after fallback or corrupt data, requiring callers to abandon or discount later frames, with loop protection on non-advancing stacks.

Video setup retries indefinitely until a mode is accepted, interactive entry restricts to alphanumerics and depends on ticking seconds for timeout progress, so stalled firmware clock or repeated invalid choices can delay boot.
